headline: Count-based and sequence models map regulatory variant effects across cell types
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Modeling
summary: Donor-level expression and chromatin data now support genetic effect models that capture cell-type structure and noncoding variant impact.
synthesis: The dominant thread is fitting genetic-effect models to donor- and cell-type-level structure, and scoring variants from sequence. jaxQTL applies negative binomial count models to pseudobulk single-cell eQTL mapping and reports more eGenes than linear models, including distal ones. PrediXSKAT embeds PrediXcan-predicted gene expression into the SKAT kernel to jointly model rare coding and common cis-regulatory variants in association testing. ChromBPNet scores 302,830 noncoding variants across 17 hematopoietic cell types, with lineage-structured accessibility effects described as complementary to GWAS. Evo2VED provides precomputed Evo2 variant effect scores for 6.48M gnomAD variants. What is new is the combination of count-aware modeling, joint coding and regulatory testing, and lineage-resolved variant scoring.
